Even during those few weeks, though, I was still hearing that voice at night and feeling like people were against me.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned a brief period last summer where you felt slightly better, can you tell me more about what was different during that time and if you experienced any significant changes in your daily life or thoughts?\n\nPatient: During those few weeks last summer, the crushing sadness and numbness lifted, so my mood felt a bit lighter. However, even though I felt better mood-wise, I was still hearing that harsh voice at night and remained completely convinced that people were secretly sharing warnings and blacklisting me. The paranoia and the voice didn't go away at all, even when the depression did.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe this 'harsh voice' you hear at night in more detail, such as what it says and how often you hear it?\n\nPatient: It sounds a bit like my ex-husband but much harsher, and I hear it almost every night when the apartment gets quiet. It tells me that I’m a fraud, that my art hurts people, and that I should just disappear. It’s so clear and loud that I catch myself answering it out loud sometimes.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about when you hear this voice, is it only at night or do you hear it during the day as well, and does it ever tell you to do anything specific?\n\nPatient: I hear it pretty much every day, but it’s definitely loudest and most clear at night when the apartment gets quiet. It doesn't tell me to do specific tasks, but it constantly tells me that I'm a fraud, that my art hurts people, and that I should just disappear.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about the voice you hear, such as whether it comments on your thoughts or actions, or if it talks to you in a conversational manner?\n\nPatient: It doesn't really have a back-and-forth conversation with me, but it directly addresses me and insults everything I do. It mostly just criticizes my actions, constantly telling me that my art is harmful and that I'm a fraud. It is so loud and direct that I find myself talking back to it, trying to defend myself.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever seen anything unusual or had visions that other people can't see, in addition to hearing the harsh voice?\n\nPatient: No, I've never seen anything unusual or had any kind of visions like that. The experience is really just limited to hearing that harsh voice, especially when it gets quiet at night. I don't see things that others can't see.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe that people are actually talking about you or plotting against you when you hear this voice, or do you think it's just your own thoughts or conscience?\n\nPatient: It doesn't feel like my own thoughts at all; it is a very real, distinct voice that sounds like it's coming from outside my head. I absolutely believe they are plotting against me, because I'm convinced people from the museum and my soccer league are blacklisting me online. Even though my friend says it's impossible, every missed email or unreturned call feels like proof that they're all in on it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the beliefs about people plotting against you could be a product of your own mind, or do you believe they are absolutely real and coming from outside yourself?\n\nPatient: Honestly, I'm so confused because my friend and my ex keep telling me it's impossible, and I've reached a point where I don't even trust my own mind anymore. But when it's happening, it feels so incredibly real and convincing that I just can't shake the feeling that the voice is real and they really are blacklisting me.\n\nDoctor: When you're not hearing the voice or feeling the intense guilt, do you ever think that maybe your beliefs about being a fraud or people plotting against you might not be entirely true, or do you still hold onto those beliefs as factual?\n\nPatient: Even when my mood lifted last summer and I wasn't feeling as depressed, I still held onto those beliefs as absolute facts. I just can't shake the feeling that they are blacklisting me, and every missed email or unreturned call feels like proof. No matter what my friend or my ex says to reassure me, I remain completely convinced they are secretly sharing warnings about me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situations or times when you've had these beliefs about being blacklisted or the voice telling you to disappear, and then later found out that they weren't true or that there was a more rational explanation for what was happening?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never really had a moment where I realized these things weren't true. Even though my ex and my friend tell me the blacklisting is impossible, every unanswered email just makes me feel like it's completely real. That voice at night is also just too loud and clear to ever explain away rationally.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or situations that could possibly prove to you that the voice and the beliefs about being blacklisted are not real, or are these beliefs absolute and unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: They feel completely absolute and unshakeable to me because everything is just too real to ignore. Even though my ex and my friend tell me it's impossible, I can't help but see every missed email as proof of the blacklisting. The voice is also so loud and clear at night that I catch myself talking back to it, so I can't imagine any evidence that would change my mind.\n\nDoctor: When you're experiencing these intense feelings of guilt and hearing the voice, do you think that these thoughts and voices are a part of your own mind, or do you believe they are coming from an external source and are a real reflection of how others see you?\n\nPatient: I believe they are coming from an external source and are a real reflection of how others see me. The voice is so clear and external, like a harsher version of my ex-husband, and I genuinely believe the online blacklisting is actually happening. It feels entirely real to me rather than just part of my own mind, even though everyone else tells me it's not possible.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever have moments where you question whether your perceptions of being blacklisted and the voice you hear might be a distorted view of reality, or do you always believe them to be true reflections of the world?\n\nPatient: I feel deeply conflicted because, on one hand, I’ve reached a point where I don't trust my own mind and know logically that others say it's impossible. But on the other hand, the belief feels completely real and inescapable in the moment; the voice is just so clear, and every missed email feels like absolute proof of the blacklisting that I can't shake.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you differentiate between the voice you hear and your own self-criticism, especially when it comes to feelings of guilt and worthlessness?\n\nPatient: The voice is very distinct and feels completely external, like a real, harsh male voice speaking to me from the quiet of my room to tell me I'm a fraud who should disappear. My own self-criticism is different—it's an internal, heavy loop of my own thoughts where I constantly replay my past mistakes and feel this deep, quiet guilt that I've poisoned everyone's lives.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any periods where the voice stopped or significantly reduced in intensity, and if so, what was happening in your life during those times?"

I've just let everyone down so badly, and I feel like I should just stay out of everyone's way.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what specifically makes you feel like you've ruined everything and don't deserve to be doing the things you enjoy?\n\nPatient: I just constantly replay all my mistakes, like my failed marriage and dropping out of my art-education training program. I feel like I poisoned the spaces I worked in and let everyone down so badly that I don't deserve to do art or see my friends anymore. It feels like staying out of everyone's way is the only way to punish myself for how much I've ruined.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation recently where you felt this overwhelming sense of guilt or self-blame, and how it affected your daily activities or interactions with others?\n\nPatient: Last week, a close friend called to invite me to a local art show, but I just stared at the phone and couldn't bring myself to answer because I felt too ashamed to be around anyone. I ended up just lying on the couch, ignoring her and letting my rent bills pile up, because I feel like I don't deserve to have a normal life or friends anymore.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been feeling this intense guilt and self-blame, and has it been constant or have you had any periods where you felt somewhat better?\n\nPatient: These feelings really settled in midway through the first year after my divorce, so it's been well over a year of feeling like this almost constantly. There was just a brief period last summer for a few weeks where the heavy sadness lifted slightly and I didn't feel quite as numb. Even during those few weeks, though, I was still hearing that voice at night and feeling like people were against me.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned a brief period last summer where you felt slightly better, can you tell me more about what was different during that time and if you experienced any significant changes in your daily life or thoughts?\n\nPatient: During those few weeks last summer, the crushing sadness and numbness lifted, so my mood felt a bit lighter. However, even though I felt better mood-wise, I was still hearing that harsh voice at night and remained completely convinced that people were secretly sharing warnings and blacklisting me. The paranoia and the voice didn't go away at all, even when the depression did.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe this 'harsh voice' you hear at night in more detail, such as what it says and how often you hear it?\n\nPatient: It sounds a bit like my ex-husband but much harsher, and I hear it almost every night when the apartment gets quiet. It tells me that I’m a fraud, that my art hurts people, and that I should just disappear. It’s so clear and loud that I catch myself answering it out loud sometimes.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about when you hear this voice, is it only at night or do you hear it during the day as well, and does it ever tell you to do anything specific?\n\nPatient: I hear it pretty much every day, but it’s definitely loudest and most clear at night when the apartment gets quiet. It doesn't tell me to do specific tasks, but it constantly tells me that I'm a fraud, that my art hurts people, and that I should just disappear.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about the voice you hear, such as whether it comments on your thoughts or actions, or if it talks to you in a conversational manner?\n\nPatient: It doesn't really have a back-and-forth conversation with me, but it directly addresses me and insults everything I do. It mostly just criticizes my actions, constantly telling me that my art is harmful and that I'm a fraud. It is so loud and direct that I find myself talking back to it, trying to defend myself.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever seen anything unusual or had visions that other people can't see, in addition to hearing the harsh voice?\n\nPatient: No, I've never seen anything unusual or had any kind of visions like that. The experience is really just limited to hearing that harsh voice, especially when it gets quiet at night. I don't see things that others can't see.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe that people are actually talking about you or plotting against you when you hear this voice, or do you think it's just your own thoughts or conscience?\n\nPatient: It doesn't feel like my own thoughts at all; it is a very real, distinct voice that sounds like it's coming from outside my head. I absolutely believe they are plotting against me, because I'm convinced people from the museum and my soccer league are blacklisting me online. Even though my friend says it's impossible, every missed email or unreturned call feels like proof that they're all in on it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the beliefs about people plotting against you could be a product of your own mind, or do you believe they are absolutely real and coming from outside yourself?\n\nPatient: Honestly, I'm so confused because my friend and my ex keep telling me it's impossible, and I've reached a point where I don't even trust my own mind anymore. But when it's happening, it feels so incredibly real and convincing that I just can't shake the feeling that the voice is real and they really are blacklisting me.\n\nDoctor: When you're not hearing the voice or feeling the intense guilt, do you ever think that maybe your beliefs about being a fraud or people plotting against you might not be entirely true, or do you still hold onto those beliefs as factual?\n\nPatient: Even when my mood lifted last summer and I wasn't feeling as depressed, I still held onto those beliefs as absolute facts. I just can't shake the feeling that they are blacklisting me, and every missed email or unreturned call feels like proof. No matter what my friend or my ex says to reassure me, I remain completely convinced they are secretly sharing warnings about me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situations or times when you've had these beliefs about being blacklisted or the voice telling you to disappear, and then later found out that they weren't true or that there was a more rational explanation for what was happening?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never really had a moment where I realized these things weren't true. Even though my ex and my friend tell me the blacklisting is impossible, every unanswered email just makes me feel like it's completely real. That voice at night is also just too loud and clear to ever explain away rationally.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or situations that could possibly prove to you that the voice and the beliefs about being blacklisted are not real, or are these beliefs absolute and unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: They feel completely absolute and unshakeable to me because everything is just too real to ignore. Even though my ex and my friend tell me it's impossible, I can't help but see every missed email as proof of the blacklisting. The voice is also so loud and clear at night that I catch myself talking back to it, so I can't imagine any evidence that would change my mind.\n\nDoctor: When you're experiencing these intense feelings of guilt and hearing the voice, do you think that these thoughts and voices are a part of your own mind, or do you believe they are coming from an external source and are a real reflection of how others see you?\n\nPatient: I believe they are coming from an external source and are a real reflection of how others see me. The voice is so clear and external, like a harsher version of my ex-husband, and I genuinely believe the online blacklisting is actually happening. It feels entirely real to me rather than just part of my own mind, even though everyone else tells me it's not possible.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever have moments where you question whether your perceptions of being blacklisted and the voice you hear might be a distorted view of reality, or do you always believe them to be true reflections of the world?\n\nPatient: I feel deeply conflicted because, on one hand, I’ve reached a point where I don't trust my own mind and know logically that others say it's impossible. But on the other hand, the belief feels completely real and inescapable in the moment; the voice is just so clear, and every missed email feels like absolute proof of the blacklisting that I can't shake.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you differentiate between the voice you hear and your own self-criticism, especially when it comes to feelings of guilt and worthlessness?\n\nPatient: The voice is very distinct and feels completely external, like a real, harsh male voice speaking to me from the quiet of my room to tell me I'm a fraud who should disappear. My own self-criticism is different—it's an internal, heavy loop of my own thoughts where I constantly replay my past mistakes and feel this deep, quiet guilt that I've poisoned everyone's lives.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any periods where the voice stopped or significantly reduced in intensity, and if so, what was happening in your life during those times?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced any periods where the voice stopped or got much better since it first started. It has been pretty constant, even during those few weeks last summer when my mood lifted slightly. It just seems to stay with me almost every night, no matter what is going on in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that could ever make you question or change your belief that the voice you hear and the perceived blacklisting are real, or are these beliefs unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: They feel completely unshakeable to me; even though my ex-husband and a close friend have tried to convince me it's impossible, I can't shake the feeling because every missed email or unanswered call feels like direct proof. On top of that, the voice is just too loud, clear, and real to doubt, making it feel impossible to question.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation where you might consider the possibility that your beliefs about the voice and the blacklisting could be incorrect, even if it feels absolutely real to you right now?"

I ended up just lying on the couch, ignoring her and letting my rent bills pile up, because I feel like I don't deserve to have a normal life or friends anymore.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been feeling this intense guilt and self-blame, and has it been constant or have you had any periods where you felt somewhat better?\n\nPatient: These feelings really settled in midway through the first year after my divorce, so it's been well over a year of feeling like this almost constantly. There was just a brief period last summer for a few weeks where the heavy sadness lifted slightly and I didn't feel quite as numb. Even during those few weeks, though, I was still hearing that voice at night and feeling like people were against me.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned a brief period last summer where you felt slightly better, can you tell me more about what was different during that time and if you experienced any significant changes in your daily life or thoughts?\n\nPatient: During those few weeks last summer, the crushing sadness and numbness lifted, so my mood felt a bit lighter. However, even though I felt better mood-wise, I was still hearing that harsh voice at night and remained completely convinced that people were secretly sharing warnings and blacklisting me. The paranoia and the voice didn't go away at all, even when the depression did.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe this 'harsh voice' you hear at night in more detail, such as what it says and how often you hear it?\n\nPatient: It sounds a bit like my ex-husband but much harsher, and I hear it almost every night when the apartment gets quiet. It tells me that I’m a fraud, that my art hurts people, and that I should just disappear. It’s so clear and loud that I catch myself answering it out loud sometimes.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about when you hear this voice, is it only at night or do you hear it during the day as well, and does it ever tell you to do anything specific?\n\nPatient: I hear it pretty much every day, but it’s definitely loudest and most clear at night when the apartment gets quiet. It doesn't tell me to do specific tasks, but it constantly tells me that I'm a fraud, that my art hurts people, and that I should just disappear.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about the voice you hear, such as whether it comments on your thoughts or actions, or if it talks to you in a conversational manner?\n\nPatient: It doesn't really have a back-and-forth conversation with me, but it directly addresses me and insults everything I do. It mostly just criticizes my actions, constantly telling me that my art is harmful and that I'm a fraud. It is so loud and direct that I find myself talking back to it, trying to defend myself.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever seen anything unusual or had visions that other people can't see, in addition to hearing the harsh voice?\n\nPatient: No, I've never seen anything unusual or had any kind of visions like that. The experience is really just limited to hearing that harsh voice, especially when it gets quiet at night. I don't see things that others can't see.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe that people are actually talking about you or plotting against you when you hear this voice, or do you think it's just your own thoughts or conscience?\n\nPatient: It doesn't feel like my own thoughts at all; it is a very real, distinct voice that sounds like it's coming from outside my head. I absolutely believe they are plotting against me, because I'm convinced people from the museum and my soccer league are blacklisting me online. Even though my friend says it's impossible, every missed email or unreturned call feels like proof that they're all in on it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the beliefs about people plotting against you could be a product of your own mind, or do you believe they are absolutely real and coming from outside yourself?\n\nPatient: Honestly, I'm so confused because my friend and my ex keep telling me it's impossible, and I've reached a point where I don't even trust my own mind anymore. But when it's happening, it feels so incredibly real and convincing that I just can't shake the feeling that the voice is real and they really are blacklisting me.\n\nDoctor: When you're not hearing the voice or feeling the intense guilt, do you ever think that maybe your beliefs about being a fraud or people plotting against you might not be entirely true, or do you still hold onto those beliefs as factual?\n\nPatient: Even when my mood lifted last summer and I wasn't feeling as depressed, I still held onto those beliefs as absolute facts. I just can't shake the feeling that they are blacklisting me, and every missed email or unreturned call feels like proof. No matter what my friend or my ex says to reassure me, I remain completely convinced they are secretly sharing warnings about me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situations or times when you've had these beliefs about being blacklisted or the voice telling you to disappear, and then later found out that they weren't true or that there was a more rational explanation for what was happening?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never really had a moment where I realized these things weren't true. Even though my ex and my friend tell me the blacklisting is impossible, every unanswered email just makes me feel like it's completely real. That voice at night is also just too loud and clear to ever explain away rationally.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or situations that could possibly prove to you that the voice and the beliefs about being blacklisted are not real, or are these beliefs absolute and unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: They feel completely absolute and unshakeable to me because everything is just too real to ignore. Even though my ex and my friend tell me it's impossible, I can't help but see every missed email as proof of the blacklisting. The voice is also so loud and clear at night that I catch myself talking back to it, so I can't imagine any evidence that would change my mind.\n\nDoctor: When you're experiencing these intense feelings of guilt and hearing the voice, do you think that these thoughts and voices are a part of your own mind, or do you believe they are coming from an external source and are a real reflection of how others see you?\n\nPatient: I believe they are coming from an external source and are a real reflection of how others see me. The voice is so clear and external, like a harsher version of my ex-husband, and I genuinely believe the online blacklisting is actually happening. It feels entirely real to me rather than just part of my own mind, even though everyone else tells me it's not possible.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever have moments where you question whether your perceptions of being blacklisted and the voice you hear might be a distorted view of reality, or do you always believe them to be true reflections of the world?\n\nPatient: I feel deeply conflicted because, on one hand, I’ve reached a point where I don't trust my own mind and know logically that others say it's impossible. But on the other hand, the belief feels completely real and inescapable in the moment; the voice is just so clear, and every missed email feels like absolute proof of the blacklisting that I can't shake.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you differentiate between the voice you hear and your own self-criticism, especially when it comes to feelings of guilt and worthlessness?\n\nPatient: The voice is very distinct and feels completely external, like a real, harsh male voice speaking to me from the quiet of my room to tell me I'm a fraud who should disappear. My own self-criticism is different—it's an internal, heavy loop of my own thoughts where I constantly replay my past mistakes and feel this deep, quiet guilt that I've poisoned everyone's lives.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any periods where the voice stopped or significantly reduced in intensity, and if so, what was happening in your life during those times?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced any periods where the voice stopped or got much better since it first started. It has been pretty constant, even during those few weeks last summer when my mood lifted slightly. It just seems to stay with me almost every night, no matter what is going on in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that could ever make you question or change your belief that the voice you hear and the perceived blacklisting are real, or are these beliefs unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: They feel completely unshakeable to me; even though my ex-husband and a close friend have tried to convince me it's impossible, I can't shake the feeling because every missed email or unanswered call feels like direct proof. On top of that, the voice is just too loud, clear, and real to doubt, making it feel impossible to question.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation where you might consider the possibility that your beliefs about the voice and the blacklisting could be incorrect, even if it feels absolutely real to you right now?\n\nPatient: It’s almost impossible for me to imagine a scenario where this isn't true, because even though my ex and my friend insist it's not happening, it just feels too incredibly real to doubt. Every missed email or unreturned call feels like direct proof of the blacklisting, and the voice at night is so loud and clear that I can't help but believe it. I just can't see how it could all be incorrect when everything points to it being real.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief in the voice and the blacklisting affects your daily life and interactions, and do you think it's possible that these beliefs might be influencing your feelings of guilt and worthlessness?\n\nPatient: Believing I'm blacklisted and hearing that voice makes me isolate myself completely, so I ignore my friends and have stopped doing art or showing up to anything. They absolutely feed into my guilt, because hearing that I'm a fraud who hurts people makes me feel like I really did poison my old workspaces. It makes me feel like I deserve to be completely isolated as a punishment.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you think your life would change if you were to stop believing the voice and the idea that you're being blacklisted, and do you think that would affect your feelings of guilt and worthlessness?\n\nPatient: It is so hard to even imagine not believing them because they feel so terrifyingly real, but if I could somehow stop, maybe I wouldn't feel so completely cut off and afraid. But those things directly fuel my intense guilt and the feeling that I'm a poison to others, so they are hard to separate. Even without them, though, I think I would still feel heavily weighed down by my real-world failures, like my divorce and dropping out of my training program.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and your beliefs about being blacklisted would change or go away if you were in a completely different environment, like a new city or a hospital, or do you believe they would remain the same?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, and I haven't really thought about whether a different place would change things. But because the voice and the feeling of being blacklisted feel so constant and incredibly real, it's hard to imagine them just going away.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and your feelings of guilt would change if someone you trust, like a close friend or family member, were to tell you that they believe in you and your abilities, and that they think you're being too hard on yourself?\n\nPatient: While I really appreciate it when my friend or my ex tries to reassure me, it ultimately doesn't change how I feel. The voice and this deep sense of guilt are just too powerful to be shaken by kind words, and I still feel like a fraud who has ruined everything. I often just end up thinking they are being nice to me or that they simply don't see the truth about what I've done.\n\nDoctor: When you're hearing the voice or feeling like you're being blacklisted, do you ever think that this might be related to your own feelings of guilt and shame about your past mistakes, rather than an actual plot against you?\n\nPatient: I do carry an overwhelming amount of guilt and constantly replay my mistakes, feeling like I deserve some kind of punishment. But despite that, the voice and the online blacklisting feel terrifyingly real to me, almost like they are the actual real-world consequence of how badly I've messed up. Even though my friend says it's impossible, I just can't shake the feeling that this plot is actually happening to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or situation that could possibly prove to you that your guilt and self-blame are not entirely deserved, or are these feelings absolute and unshakeable for you?\n\nPatient: No, they feel completely absolute and unshakeable to me. I can't think of any evidence to the contrary, because staying out of everyone's way feels like a necessary punishment for what I've done.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you would feel and what you would think if someone presented you with concrete evidence that there is no online blacklisting against you and that the voice you hear is a product of your own mind, would that change your beliefs or feelings of guilt?\n\nPatient: While I really want to believe that, it is incredibly hard to shake these thoughts because every missed email or quiet moment makes the blacklisting and the voice feel completely real again. Even if someone could somehow prove they weren't real, the deep sense of guilt, worthlessness, and the feeling that I've ruined my life and deserve to be isolated would still weigh heavily on me.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there are times when you feel like the voice and the beliefs about being blacklisted are not real, but the feelings of guilt and worthlessness about your past mistakes are still present, or are these two things always connected for you?\n\nPatient: While the voice, the paranoia, and the heavy depression feel tangled together most of the time, the feelings of guilt and worthlessness are much more constant. Even if the voice quiets down or the blacklisting fears feel slightly less intense, that crushing sense of regret and having ruined my life is almost always there in the background.
